analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Distributed/). I found no production code, key handling, attestation, coordinator WebSocket, cache-storage or privilege changes.

ClusterPairServingDecisionsTests.swift (head line 158): the test call to ClusterPairServingGrants.publicTrafficLine now passes publicModels: [], isolating the records-only decision from the owner's public-model declaration. This implies a production signature change, and a ClusterPublicModels declaration mechanism, that is not in the supplied diff. The new semantics are not verifiable from this batch: whether an owner declaration alone can grant public traffic without a qualification record, or how it interacts with record-derived grants. Existing assertions still cover diverged records withholding public grants (lines 58-105, 140-183).

DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift adds the following.
- fixture(artifact:) and assistantQuote(artifact:assistant:) parameters (head lines 47-51, 828-841).
- inlineAssistantArtifact(), extracted by refactor (head lines 727-748).
- A test that discoveryMode(.auto, coordinator: true) == .off. Under the default auto setting, a coordinator-served cluster does not request Qwen's speculative assistant; only an explicit .on does (head lines 769-788). This is a conservative default and implies a production change.
- A test that a plan with tensorAssistant is reported as 'not offered for public traffic' (ClusterPairOwnerServing.tensorAssistantNotOffered), while a plan without the assistant is 'qualified for public traffic in tensor parallel mode' (head lines 929-969).
- An onLargeStack helper using a Thread plus a semaphore (head lines 1083-1097). It is test-only, with an @unchecked Sendable box that is written before the signal and read after the wait.

Threat-model relevance: T-052 and T-056 (overclaiming qualification or public eligibility) and T-054 (qualified artifact identity). The tests reinforce fail-closed, honest reporting rather than weakening it. The production implementations (ClusterSetupPlanning.decide, ClusterPublicModels, ClusterConfiguration.validate, discoveryMode) are outside the supplied evidence. A later pass should check that the public-traffic line cannot be shown as qualified when the coordinator-paired configuration drops the assistant, and that ClusterPublicModels declarations are bound to the artifact SHA-256 digest.
